title: Some thoughts on Le Cam's statistical decision theory
comment: Unpublished paper written in 2000, shortly after Le Cam's death. "In correspondence during the summer of 1990, I discussed some of the ideas appearing in this paper with Lucien Le Cam. Even when he disagreed with my suggestions, or when I was "discovering" results that were already in his 1986 book or earlier work, he was invariably gracious, encouraging and helpful."
abstract: The paper contains some musings about the abstractions introduced by Lucien Le Cam into the asymptotic theory of statistical inference and decision theory. A short, self-contained proof of a key result (existence of randomizations via convergence in distribution of likelihood ratios), and an outline of a proof of a local asymptotic minimax theorem, are presented as an illustration of how Le Cam's approach leads to conceptual simplifications of asymptotic theory.
